packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-18 - unverified blind image reading

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- No proposed identification of this text was in my context. A modern pencil
  note on the leaf itself reads "Stams, STA / Inq. 254-1r" (bottom of the
  upright recto, image-003); that is a holding/shelfmark note, not a text
  identification.
- Beyond the brief: the harness refused to display the original image files
  directly ("request limit"), including the overviews image-001, image-002 and
  image-010, which I therefore never saw. I instead made enhanced, enlarged
  crops of the native tiles (image-003 to image-009, image-011 to image-018)
  with a small local script in the session scratchpad and read those. Tiles
  image-003 to image-009 appeared upside down; I rotated them 180 degrees.
  Line numbers below are therefore counted from the top of the UPRIGHT
  (rotated) tile, and are approximate (counted on my enlarged thirds of each
  tile, merged with overlap removed). image-016 was cropped but not read
  closely.
- No web, search, catalogue or edition used. packet.json not opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations from tiles only; no overview seen)
- Recto (tiles 003-009): one narrow column of a small gothic book hand, dark
  brown ink, heavy abbreviation; text column runs to the right edge of the
  fragment (cut off at right, so every line is truncated; only the first
  ~10-15 letters of each line survive). Wide left margin. Red and blue
  alternating paraphs with long penwork tails; a run of small two-colour
  (red/blue split) initials R, N(?), R, B, E, H, P, T, P stacked down the
  left edge of the column. Small black letters a, b, c, d, e, f in the left
  margin with a hooked stroke, set against new sections (reference letters).
  A ruled red+blue frame (box) encloses one block of text in tile 009/007.
  Faint cursive marginal notes in a later hand in the left margin (tiles
  009, 007, 003). Many lines contain "l." "S." "ff." "c." style reference
  abbreviations - looks like legal text with allegations (tentative
  interpretation; not inferred author/work).
- Verso (tiles 011-018): largely abraded/blank. Top (image-011): ruled
  red/blue penwork frame and the right-hand ends of a few column lines in
  faded brown; a note in the upper right margin, roughly "p(ro)? uiii"
  [uncertain]. Down the left edge only line-endings of the column survive
  (image-011, image-018). A later cursive note block (~18 lines) in the
  middle/lower part (image-012) and smaller cursive notes (image-013,
  image-015). Faint blue/red ghost paraphs/initials (image-014) - possibly
  offset from the facing side (interpretation).
- Order of recto tiles inferred from overlapping lines:
  chain A = 008 (leaf top edge visible) -> 006 -> 004;
  chain B = 009 -> 007 -> 005 -> 003 (leaf bottom edge with pencil note).
  How chain A's end joins chain B's start is NOT established (004 ends in a
  faded area); treat A then B as provisional.

AREAS SELECTED: the whole surviving recto column (truncated line-starts),
because no line survives in full. Verso: cursive note in image-012 attempted
in part; image-013 note in part. UNREAD: most of the verso cursive notes;
recto marginal cursive notes only partly; very faded lines in 005/007 lower.
Suggest: an un-truncated/adjacent piece of the same leaf (right part of the
column) and UV/multispectral for the verso.

CONVENTIONS: (x) expansion; word? = uncertain; [illegible]; [...] = line
continues off the cut edge. "¶" = coloured paraph. Bracketed marginal letters
are the small black reference letters in the left margin.
